Indomitable

in-DOM-ih-tuh-bul -- Latin in- ('not') + domitare ('to tame'). · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Indomitable is impossible to subdue, defeat, or discourage.

The small fishing village's indomitable spirit kept it rebuilding after every single hurricane season.

Worked Example

Even after being voted out of student council twice, she ran again the following year with the same indomitable determination.

That refusal to be discouraged or defeated, no matter how many setbacks pile up, is exactly what indomitable describes.

How Indomitable Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unyielding

unyielding: firm and refusing to change or give in

unconquerable

unconquerable: impossible to overcome under any circumstances

Antonyms

yielding

yielding: giving in easily to pressure

fainthearted

fainthearted: lacking courage or resolve

How Strong Is It? — unyielding → indomitable → unconquerable

unyielding vs. indomitable

unyielding vs. indomitable: The negotiator remained unyielding on the price no matter how many times the buyer pushed back.

unconquerable vs. indomitable

unconquerable vs. indomitable: For centuries, the fortress was considered unconquerable, its walls never once breached.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — in-

prefix — in-: not (Latin)

root — -domit-

root — -domit-: to tame, master (Latin (domare))

suffix — -able

suffix — -able: able to be, capable of being (Latin (-abilis))

Put it together

Put it together: Latin in- ('not') plus domare ('to tame') plus -able ('able to be') -- indomitable literally means 'not able to be tamed' or mastered.

Use the root in a new word: dominate

Use the root in a new word: dominate: The home team began to dominate the second half, scoring three unanswered goals.

Word Choice

Indomitable almost always describes a spirit, will, or determination that survives real hardship -- it's a strong, admiring word, rarely used sarcastically.
